card.title: Fuel
card.noTank: Set up the tank to see the level, consumption and efficiency.
card.noLevel: The device hasn't sent the level in the last 7 days.
card.noSensor: No level sensor: consumption is estimated from the expected rate.

problems.capacity: Enter the tank capacity, in liters.
problems.calibrationPoints: The calibration table needs at least two points.
problems.calibrationRepeated: Two rows in the table have the same reading.
problems.normPositive: Expected consumption rates must be numbers greater than zero.
problems.needSource: Choose the level sensor value or enter at least one expected consumption rate.

config.removeBody: The tank of {{name}} will be removed: the level and consumption will no longer show. Positions aren't touched, so setting it up again brings everything back.
config.sensorNote: If the GPS device measures fuel, choose which of the values it sends is the level.
config.noSensor: This vehicle has no level sensor
config.noAttrs: The device hasn't sent data yet. Once it reports, the values will show up here to choose from.
config.calibrationLead: Calibration table: for each sensor reading, how many liters are in the tank. You build it by filling the tank in steps and noting the reading at each point.
config.normNote: Optional. It's used to estimate how much it should have used and compare it with what the sensor measured.
config.counterNote: Some devices read from the vehicle's computer how much fuel the engine has used. It's the most accurate value: if you choose it, actual consumption comes from there.

report.idleSensorNorm: {{liters}} L by the sensor · {{norm}} L expected
report.costNone: record a fill-up with its total
report.paidNone: no fill-ups recorded with a total
report.theft: Possible fuel theft: fuel left the tank with the engine off. Check the drains below.
report.noLevel: No level readings in this period.
report.noLevelNorm: No level readings in this period: the consumption you see is the expected one.
report.drainOff: Drain of <num>{{liters}}</num> L with the engine off
report.drainOn: Drain of <num>{{liters}}</num> L with the engine on
report.compareSame: It used what the expected rate says.
report.compareMore: It used {{percent}} % more than the expected rate.
report.compareLess: It used {{percent}} % less than the expected rate.

chart.note: Liters in the tank. Rises are fuel loads; a sharp drop while stopped is a drain.

fills.title: {{name}} fill-ups
fills.removeBody: The record of {{liters}} L on {{when}} will be deleted. If the sensor detected that load, it will still show as detected but not recorded.
fills.empty: No fill-ups in this period. The ones you record or import show up here, along with the loads the tank sensor detects.
fills.periodTotalPaid: Recorded in the period: {{liters}} L for {{paid}}.
fills.detectedOnly: Detected by the sensor, not recorded
fills.mismatch: <num>{{recorded}}</num> L were recorded, but the tank rose <num>{{detected}}</num> L: <num>{{missing}}</num> L are missing.

problems.date: Enter the date and time of the fill-up.
problems.numbers: The total and the odometer are numbers.

fills.seed: The sensor detected the tank rose <num>{{liters}}</num> L. Correct the liters if the receipt says otherwise: the difference stays visible.
fills.noteHint: For example, the voucher or invoice number.

import.title: Import fill-ups
import.lead: Upload a CSV file, like the one a spreadsheet exports or a fuel card provides. The first row holds the headers. Vehicle (its name or plate), Date and Liters are required; Time, Total, Currency, Odometer, Station and Note are read too. It works for all the account's vehicles at once.
import.repeated_one: {{count}} was already recorded and wasn't repeated.
import.repeated_other: {{count}} were already recorded and weren't repeated.

settings.title: Account fuel settings
settings.who: Who gets alerted about possible fuel theft is set in Administration → Notifications.
